The four lines containing its sides are  

\[
x=0,\qquad x=1,\qquad y=0,\qquad y=1 .
\]

For a point \(P=(x,y)\) the distances to these lines are  

\[
d_{1}=|x|,\qquad d_{2}=|x-1|,\qquad d_{3}=|y|,\qquad d_{4}=|y-1|.
\]

Hence the condition “the sum of the distances to the four lines equals 4’’ is  

\[
|x|+|x-1|+|y|+|y-1|=4. \tag{1}
\]

---

### 1.  Reduce the equation

Define  

\[
f(t)=|t|+|t-1|=
\begin{cases}
1-2t, & t<0,\\[2pt]
1,    & 0\le t\le 1,\\[2pt]
2t-1, & t>1 .
\end{cases}
\]

Then (1) becomes  

\[
f(x)+f(y)=4. \tag{2}
\]

Because \(f(t)\ge 1\) for all \(t\), both \(f(x)\) and \(f(y)\) must lie in \([1,\infty)\) and their sum must be \(4\).
Thus each of \(x\) and \(y\) is either inside the interval \([0,1]\) (where \(f=1\)) or outside it, where \(f\) is linear.

| \(x<0,\;y<0\) | \((1-2x)+(1-2y)=2-2x-2y\) | \(x+y=-1\) | \(\{(t,-1-t): -1\le t\le0\}\) |
| \(x>1,\;y>1\) | \((2x-1)+(2y-1)=2x+2y-2\) | \(x+y=3\) | \(\{(t,3-t): 1\le t\le2\}\) |
| \(x<0,\;y>1\) | \((1-2x)+(2y-1)=2(y-x)\) | \(y-x=2\) | \(\{(t,t+2): -1\le t\le0\}\) |
| \(x>1,\;y<0\) | \((2x-1)+(1-2y)=2(x-y)\) | \(x-y=2\) | \(\{(t,t-2): 1\le t\le2\}\) |

All the obtained sets satisfy (1) and together they give the complete solution.

---

### 3.  Description of the solution set  

The eight families of points obtained above are exactly the eight edges of the convex octagon whose vertices are  

\[
(-1,0),\;(0,-1),\;(1,-1),\;(2,0),\;(2,1),\;(1,2),\;(0,2),\;(-1,1).
\]

Thus the set of all points whose sum of distances to the four lines of the unit square equals 4 is the boundary of this octagon.

\[
\boxed{\;
\begin{aligned}
&\{(-1,y):0\le y\le1\}\cup\{(2,y):0\le y\le1\}\cup\{(x,-1):0\le x\le1\}\cup\{(x,2):0\le x\le1\}\\
&\cup\{(t,-1-t): -1\le t\le0\}\cup\{(t,3-t):1\le t\le2\}\cup\{(t,t+2): -1\le t\le0\}\cup\{(t,t-2):1\le t\le2\}
\end{aligned}
\;}
\]

Equivalently, it is the octagon with vertices  

\[
(-1,0),\;(0,-1),\;(1,-1),\;(2,0),\;(2,1),\;(1,2),\;(0,2),\;(-1,1).
\]<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
